question: What will be the combined voteshare of PP and PSOE in the 2026 Spanish General Election?

calls.reasoning: October 2026 private polls put PP ~28.5-33 and PSOE ~25-28, combined ~55.6-59.4; poll-of-polls ~32+26=58, PolitPro 30.6+26.2=56.8. CIS outlier (PSOE 34, PP 22.2 = 56.2) discounted. PSOE trending up, PP slightly down, Vox rising, so the combined share is roughly flat. Historically the two majors sometimes gain on polls via late tactical consolidation (2023: polls ~62, result 64.8), but in April 2019 they fell short. Median set slightly above the poll average at 58.2, SD ~3. No human market prices the combined share; Polymarket most-seats contracts (PP 0.84, PSOE 0.15) only confirm PP leads and are near-miss evidence, not an anchor. No mechanism found for an escape outside 45-70.
calls.dossier:
- Election date: 29 Nov 2026 snap Congress election, called by Sanchez after housing reform collapse / housing protests (The Local 26 Oct 2026; PolitPro).
- Event window: single election day 29 Nov 2026; resolves off the official/most complete Congress results before 2027; as of 31 Oct 2026 the vote has not happened (0% of the count in).
- Resolves off national Congress vote share; PSOE includes PSC; PP includes PP-led coalitions (e.g. PP-Foro, PP+UPN alliances count).
- Wikipedia poll table (Oct 2026), PP/PSOE: PSOE internal 25 Oct 29.0/30.0; SocioMetrica 1-25 Oct 32.4/27.0; NC Report 22-24 Oct 33.1/25.8; Winston 21-23 Oct 29.4/27.1; EM-Analytics 17-23 Oct 30.9/26.7; Ateneo del Dato 20-22 Oct 31.1/27.6; Sigma Dos 8-22 Oct 30.6/26.1; IMOP 13-16 Oct 28.5/27.1; Sigma Dos 1-14 Oct 31.5/25.3; SocioMetrica 10-11 Oct 32.6/26.2; Target Point 6-9 Oct 32.0/25.9; 40dB 7-8 Oct 31.9/28.1; GESOP 6-8 Oct 28.7/26.1.
- Vox ~18.6-20.0 across pollsters; Frente Amplio/Sumar ~5-9; Podemos 0.3-3.4.
- Politico poll of polls (via The Local 26 Oct): PP ~32, PSOE ~26, Vox ~19, Frente Amplio ~7.
- PolitPro average (late Oct): PP 30.6, PSOE 26.2, Vox 18.8, Sumar 5.8.
- CIS October: PSOE 34.0, PP 22.2, Vox 17.1 (outlier vs all private pollsters).
- Trend: PP slightly eroding, PSOE and Vox gaining (The Local; ara.cat).
- Historical comparison (forecaster recall, not fetched): 2023 final polls ~PP 34 + PSOE 28 = ~62 vs result 33.1 + 31.7 = 64.8; Apr 2019 polls ~48.5 vs result ~45.4; Nov 2019 polls ~48.5 vs result 48.8.
- Searched for: a market on the combined vote share (none found; only Polymarket most-seats/second-most-seats contracts).
calls.reference_class: Combined PP+PSOE vote share in Spanish general elections vs final-month poll averages (2015-2023)

calls.reasoning: Late-Oct polls give PP+PSOE ~56.8-58% combined (Infobae 16-poll avg 30.9+27.1=58.0; PolitPro 56.8; individual polls ~55.6-59.2). In 2015-2023 the final polls usually underestimated the two big parties (2023 +2.8, 2016 +5, 2015 +2.7, Nov 2019 ~0, Apr 2019 -2.6), and a polarised PP-vs-PSOE race could squeeze minor parties. So I shifted the median up about 1 point to ~59. Main counterargument: Vox is surging (~19-20%) and the left outside PSOE is splitting, which keeps the big-two share well below 2023's 64.8. No market prices the combined share; Polymarket only has seat-winner markets (PP most seats 0.84, ~$105k volume; PSOE 0.15, ~$151k). Those are near-miss contracts, used as evidence only, not as an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Election set for Sun 29 Nov 2026; Sánchez announced it 5 Oct 2026 after two housing decrees failed in Congress (La Moncloa, CNN Español, 5 Oct 2026).
- Infobae 27 Oct 2026: average of 16 pollsters, polls done 22-28 Oct: PP 30.9%, PSOE 27.1%, Vox 19.0% (PP+PSOE 58.0). PSOE gaining ground, PP slipping slightly, Vox stable or rising.
- PolitPro trend average 31 Oct 2026: PP 30.6, PSOE 26.2, Vox 18.8, Sumar 5.8, Podemos 2.8 (PP+PSOE 56.8).
- Individual polls (PolitPro): NC Report 24 Oct 33.1/25.8; Winston 23 Oct 29.4/27.1; Sigma Dos 22 Oct 30.6/26.1; IMOP 16 Oct 28.5/27.1; SocioMétrica 11 Oct 32.6/26.2; Hamalgama 8 Oct 33.4/25.3 (PP/PSOE).
- The Local 26 Oct 2026: GAD3 PP 31.4/PSOE 26.4/Vox 18.2; Sigma Dos 33.9/25.3/19.1; 40dB 31.9/28.1/18.9; CIS Oct PSOE 34/PP 22.2/Vox 17.1 (CIS is the outlier, historically leans PSOE); Politico poll of polls PP~32, PSOE~26, Vox~19, Frente Amplio~7.
- 2023 actual result: PP 33.1, PSOE 31.7 (combined 64.8).
- Historical final-poll error on PP+PSOE combined share (approximate, from memory): 2015 polls ~48 vs actual 50.7; 2016 ~50.5 vs 55.6; Apr 2019 ~48 vs 45.4; Nov 2019 ~48.5 vs 48.8; 2023 ~62 vs 64.8. Big two underestimated in 3 of 5, overestimated in 1. Error SD ~3 points.
- Status-quo outcome: result near the current poll average of about 57-58 combined.
- Arguments for higher: polarised two-bloc race, PSOE rallying the left vote (as happened in 2023), polls historically low on the big two.
- Arguments for lower: Vox at a record ~19-20%, left outside PSOE split (Sumar, Podemos, Frente Amplio), PP drifting down.
- Resolution: official Congress of Deputies vote share; PSOE includes PSC; PP includes PP-led coalitions (e.g. PP-Foro). Seat counts don't matter.
- Event window: election day 29 Nov 2026; resolves on results available before 2027; as of 31 Oct 2026 the campaign has ~4 weeks left.
- Searched and found no market on the combined share; Polymarket only lists seat-winner markets.
calls.reference_class: Final-month polling averages vs actual PP+PSOE combined vote share in Spanish general elections 2015-2023

calls.reasoning: Poll average (16 firms, fieldwork Oct 22-28) shows PP 30.9 + PSOE 27.1 = ~58.0%; individual polls range ~54.8-60. Historically polls have tended to underestimate the big-two combined share (2015 +2.7, 2016 +5.6, Apr2019 -2.6, Nov2019 +0.3, 2023 +2.8; mean ~+1.8, SD ~3), from late concentration of tactical votes. I partially apply that bias, for a median of ~59. Risks run both ways: PSOE squeezing Sumar/Podemos raises the total, Vox surging against PP lowers it. Market check: Polymarket only has most-seats contracts (PP 0.84, PSOE 0.15, ~$100-150k volume), with no vote-share contract, so these are evidence only. No realistic way out of the 45-70 range.

calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2015-2023: PP+PSOE combined share vs final poll average

calls.reasoning: Late-Oct 2026 polls put PP+PSOE at ~57-58 (16-firm average 30.9+27.1=58.0; PolitPro 56.8; individual polls 54.8-60; CIS outlier discounted). Polls have mostly underestimated the big two (mean ~+1.8, SD ~3 across 2015-2023), but a record Vox (~19%) and a fragmented left limit how much the vote can consolidate, so I apply only part of that bias, for a median of 58.8. PSOE gains and PP losses roughly offset. No market on the combined share; Polymarket seat contracts (PP most seats 0.84, PSOE 0.15) are near-miss evidence only.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: election 29 Nov 2026, not yet resolved, poll averages 56.8-58.0, CIS an outlier, no combined-share market. Factual dispute on the poll average (PolitPro 56.8 vs 16-firm 58.0) can't be settled without web access; both are plausible methods. I centre near the fresher, broader 58.0 and let the spread cover 56.8. Past poll-bias figures were from memory in all runs and match my own recall (2015 +2.7, 2016 +5, Apr 2019 -2.6, Nov 2019 +0.3, 2023 +2.8). Judgment: apply that bias only in part because of Vox strength and left fragmentation, giving a median of 58.8. Width 8.6 reflects poll error plus one month of drift. No escape mass priced.
